exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: A strong mission log explains every negative number — here is how one student tracked a weather balloon and a mine elevator.

traits.sample: The elevator at −45 meters is 45 meters BELOW ground level; zero is the surface, so the sign tells the direction.
traits.why: It interprets the sign instead of ignoring it.

traits.sample: The balloon rose to +120 m and the probe sank to −80 m, so the full range is 120 + 80 = 200 meters apart.
traits.why: Distances on opposite sides of zero are added with absolute values.

traits.sample: −60 is deeper than −35 because −60 < −35: on a vertical number line, lower means less.
traits.why: Comparing negatives correctly is the heart of this unit.

traits.trait: Connects depth to the real context
traits.sample: Using our NOAA-adapted illustrative intervals, −250 m lies in 200 m ≤ depth < 1,000 m, so the checkpoint is in the classroom twilight-zone model.
traits.why: The signed number is interpreted in a cited, explicitly illustrative interval with non-overlapping endpoints.
